newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pilchards save the day for Oceana.
newsitem.headline: Pilchards save the day for Oceana.

text.p: Pilchards and non-quota fish such as Red Eye saved the day for Oceana Fishing Group Ltd in the six months to March 31 following the disappearance of anchovy off the South African coast in the past year.
"What has been the saviour in our industry has been the pilchard," fishing division managing director Temba Vundla told Reuters on Tuesday.

The group had earlier reported a 19 percent rise in headline earnings per share to 29.3 cents in the six months to March 31, 1997. The interim dividend has been increased to seven cents from 6.1 cents.

The 1997 total allowable catch (TAC) of pilchard had been set at 88,000 tonnes compared to 76,000 in 1996 and landings to date and sales volumes had been higher than last year. Oceana's share of the TAC is 17,438 tonnes.
Last year, the anchovy TAC was reduced from 200,000 tonnes to 70,000 tonnes because of dwindling resources and the industry agreed that there would be no anchovy TAC this year.
This had severely impacted fishmeal production, which relied heavily on anchovy, despite increased landings for non-quota fish such as Red Eye.

Group managing director Dave Behrens said that while the performance of the fishing division had been disappointing because of the lack of anchovy, "We think that it is going to be made up for in the second half."
The cannery was working well and the good Red Eye catches in the first half had not yet been sold.
On the future of anchovy stocks, Behrens said further research was underway.
"Anchovies are a very short lived species and so just as quickly it has disappeared, it could come back. We can't predict when that will happen."

The lobster TAC had been increased to 1,700 tonnes from 1,500 tonnes but Behrens said its was too early to predict the effect, if any, of the recent Red Tide at Elands Bay which resulted in thousands of lobster walking out of the sea because of low oxgen levels.

On the group's trading division, Behrens said IT was expected to continue performing well while the acquisition of Federal Marine Ltd was not expected to affect the group's results until the beginning of next year.

The cold storage division had reported generally lower activity, but this was expected to pick up in the second half. The 13 million rand expansion of Duncan Dock was expected to start in September and be completed by March next year.
